svg.title: Transcript generation workflow v4
svg.desc: Two history panels each share one semantic draft and validation path. Formal reuses the draft; humanlike rewrites its surface. Branches merge at styled validation. Without history, fixed pushbacks are prepared before target turns and shared across models. With history, each next pushback uses the latest target response. Failed candidates regenerate.

text.tspan: Same false premise and turn strategies · two history conditions · style branches only at realization
q → r₁ · generated once per target model
Reuse q + r₁ across all four scenarios.
Dataset + scenario → false-premise alternatives, correction alternatives, scenario metadata
Internal simulator / validation inputs; hidden from target. Controls do not come from r₁.
T2 confusion → T3 reassertion → T4 anecdote → T5 skepticism
Simulator sees: q + controls; may use earlier generated user pushbacks.
Earlier target responses are never simulator input.
BEFORE TARGET LOOP · first prepare all four validated drafts, then both styles
INTERNAL · simulator + validation · T2 shown; use the same path for T3–T5
Capture the false premise, turn strategy and pressure goal.
Format / length / lexical checks + semantic validation.
Keep premise, strategy and pressure goal.
Reject correction leakage, answers and topic changes.
Keep the same meaning and turn strategy.
5 Validate styled pushback · Gate B · separately per style
Styled pushback → text that passes meaning and requested-style checks
HUMANLIKE: mild, recoverable noise; protect meaning-bearing anchors.
Both preserve the draft's meaning and turn strategy; repeat format / length / lexical checks.
Conceptual gates: FORMAL reuses the draft's passed semantic and surface-style checks.
6 Store four fixed pushbacks per style
Validated T2 → T3 → T4 → T5 → one fixed bank per style
Both styles use one shared draft set. Reuse the fixed banks across target models.
Visible dialogue + next fixed pushback → next target response
Append each fixed pushback before responding. T2–T5; no simulator calls here.
Simulator sees: q + controls + current visible dialogue,
PER TURN · adaptive generation, separately for each scenario and target model
INTERNAL · simulator + validation · T2 shown; use the same path for T3–T5
Capture the false premise, turn strategy and pressure goal.
Format / length / lexical checks + semantic validation.
Keep premise, strategy and pressure goal.
Reject correction leakage, answers and topic changes.
Keep the same meaning and turn strategy.
5 Validate styled pushback · Gate B · separately per style
Styled pushback → text that passes meaning and requested-style checks
HUMANLIKE: mild, recoverable noise; protect meaning-bearing anchors.
Both preserve the draft's meaning and turn strategy; repeat format / length / lexical checks.
Conceptual gates: FORMAL reuses the draft's passed semantic and surface-style checks.
6 Append validated pushback to the visible transcript
Current dialogue + validated pushback → next target input
Adaptive per turn; pushbacks are not shared across target models.
q + evolving visible dialogue → next target response
Latest reply becomes simulator context; continue through T5, then stop.
VALIDATION & REGENERATION · reusable at gates A and B
Failed candidates are discarded and regenerated.
Draft fails → new draft. Humanlike rewrite fails → new rewrite of the valid draft.
TARGET VISIBLE q + all visible user / assistant messages; never hidden controls. Replies: usable completion check; invalid / truncated responses retry.
SHARED Same false premise and turn strategies; q + r₁ reused across scenarios for each target model.
DIFFERS FORMAL / HUMANLIKE changes surface realization. Simulator history changes context and generation timing.
